Apache-1.1 license text, opening grant and clauses 1-5 (no source-disclosure, corresponding-source, same-license, linking, or network-use condition)

Apache-1.1 license text, opening grant (redistribution and use in source and binary forms, with or without modification, are permitted; this supports commercial and private use, distribution, and modification, but does not expressly grant sublicensing or patent rights)

Apache-1.1 license text, clauses 1-3 (source distributions retain the copyright notice, conditions, and disclaimer; binary distributions reproduce them in documentation or other materials; end-user documentation, if any, includes the prescribed ASF acknowledgment, alternatively placed in the software)

Apache-1.1 license text, opening grant and clauses 1-3 (the preservation and acknowledgment conditions attach to redistribution in source or binary form; modification alone creates no separate condition)

Apache-1.1 license text, clauses 4-5 (Apache and Apache Software Foundation endorsement, promotion, and derived-product naming restrictions) and final disclaimer paragraph (express and implied warranty disclaimer and limitation of liability)

Apache-1.1 license text, opening grant, clauses 1-5, and final disclaimer (complete-text review finds no express patent grant, patent covenant, patent-claim condition, or patent-license termination term)

Apache-1.1 license text, clauses 1-3 (copyright, conditions, and disclaimer must be preserved for source and binary redistribution, and a prescribed ASF acknowledgment must appear in end-user documentation, if any, or alternatively in the software); Apache-1.0 clause 3 versus Apache-1.1 clause 3 (the acknowledgment moved from advertising materials to documentation but remains a specific attribution burden)

Apache-1.1 metadata: deprecated=false, osi=true, and comments state that the license has been superseded by Apache License 2.0; Apache-1.1 clauses 3-5 impose a prescribed ASF acknowledgment and Apache-specific endorsement and product-name conditions that the recommendation vocabulary cannot represent losslessly; Apache-2.0 Section 3 supplies an express patent grant with patent-litigation termination absent from Apache-1.1, so version 1.1 is not a safe current general recommendation
